scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations” (preprints/Pointwise-convergence-of-triple-ergodic-averages-for-mixing-transformations-October-4-2026/pointwise-triple-ergodic-averages-mixing-transformations.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e76fd7732f10b250), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (X, F, µ) be an arbitrary probability space and let T : X → X be an invertible mixing probability preserving transformation with measurable inverse. For every triple of bounded measurable functions f1, f2, f3 : X → C, AN (f1, f2, f3)(x) −→ 3 Y j=1 Z X fj dµ for µ-almost every x as N → ∞ through all positive integers. The exceptional null set may depend on the triple of functions.
